open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 and ResourceBounds M04
open_points.text: “ResourceBounds M04 are enforced with `setrlimit` … [including] the size of a file written in the scratch” conflicts with M04, whose only fields are `wall_time_ms`, `memory_bytes`, `output_bytes` and `process_count`; `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max` is instead a release-wide A20 ceiling.
open_points.question: Is the per-file scratch limit the release constant `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`, or is it a new per-contract ResourceBounds field?
options: Add a scratch-file-size field to ResourceBounds M04

open_points.subject: A03 scratch-limit outcome
open_points.text: “the runner ignores the signal … so the write fails with an error the code can see” and “a limit hit … scratch … `resource_exhausted`” do not say how the runner learns that the limit was hit when user code catches the write error and returns conforming output; unlike rule 4 traps, no hit is recorded to the parent.
open_points.question: How is a scratch-file limit hit detected and made to win as `resource_exhausted` when the implementation catches the resulting error?
options: Record every `SIGXFSZ`/`EFBIG` event through a protected runner channel
Classify it only when it terminates or escapes from the implementation
Allow a caught limit error followed by conforming output to succeed
open_points.default_guess: Record the event through a protected runner channel and classify the execution `resource_exhausted`.

open_points.subject: A03 scratch writes and SIGXFSZ
open_points.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error” assumes behavior that user code can change through the standard library’s signal APIs, and a write crossing `RLIMIT_FSIZE` may make a partial write before a later error; A20 says over a ceiling is a failure, “never a truncation.”
open_points.question: Must the sandbox prevent code from changing `SIGXFSZ` handling and treat partial writes at the file-size boundary as a recorded limit hit, or are termination, partial files, and caught errors permitted to determine another outcome?
options: Lock or trap signal-handler changes and record any boundary hit as `resource_exhausted`
Permit normal Linux signal and partial-write behavior but still specify its outcome mapping
Treat only an uncaught `SIGXFSZ` or `EFBIG` as a limit hit
open_points.default_guess: Prevent alteration of `SIGXFSZ` handling and classify any attempted write beyond the ceiling as `resource_exhausted`, discarding the partial result.

open_points.subject: A03 runner files versus code files
open_points.text: Rule 1 limits “every file the code writes,” while rule 5 applies `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to the runner process before code loads and calls it “the size of a file written in the scratch.” The process limit also affects files the runner itself creates for loading, exchange, output, or control.
open_points.question: Which scratch files are subject to the file-size limit, and how is a limit hit by runner-owned exchange infrastructure classified?
options: All regular files written by the runner process, including exchange infrastructure
Only files opened or modified on behalf of user code
Separate runner infrastructure from the limited code process
open_points.default_guess: Separate runner infrastructure from the limited code process so only code-created scratch files consume this limit.

open_points.subject: A03 unbounded scratch directory
open_points.text: “the directory as a whole has no separate bound in this release” permits many individually bounded files, but the rules do not say what happens when their aggregate exhausts the backing filesystem or a host quota.
open_points.question: What execution outcome and kernel behavior apply when scratch creation or writing fails because aggregate scratch usage exhausts host storage rather than because one file reaches `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`?
options: Classify an uncaught storage error as `crashed` and allow a caught one to continue
Treat host-storage exhaustion as a fatal sandbox or kernel failure
open_points.default_guess: Classify the execution `resource_exhausted` and discard its outputs.
